events.title: Charles X’s ordinance
events.text: France demands 150 million francs to “compensate” former colonists, people they had enslaved included. Warships arrive with the bill; President Boyer signs. Haiti borrows 30 million francs from French bankers, who keep 6 million as commission.

events.title: The treasury is emptied
events.text: Haiti ships the coins in its treasury to France to make the first installment.

events.title: Bill cut to 90 million francs
events.text: A new treaty reduces the indemnity to 90 million francs and France recognizes Haiti’s independence. Payments continue.

events.title: The CIC loan
events.text: Haiti takes a new French loan, arranged by the bank Crédit Industriel et Commercial (CIC), to pay off the last of the original debt.

events.title: Last double-debt payment
events.text: A final small payment of interest and late fees closes the double debt. In all, the NYT counts about 112 million francs paid.

events.title: US Marines take the gold
events.text: In December 1914, US Marines carry $500,000 in gold from Haiti’s national bank to National City Bank’s vault in New York.

events.title: The US invades
events.text: The United States invades Haiti. By 1920, National City Bank owns Haiti’s national bank outright.

events.title: The 1922 loans
events.text: National City issues new US loans (Series A: $16 million in 30-year 6% bonds) that refinance Haiti’s older debts. The 1922–24 issues total $23.7 million.

events.title: The US loans are paid off
events.text: Haiti finishes repaying the foreign debt from the 1922 loans.

modernEvents.title: Aristide’s demand
modernEvents.text: President Jean-Bertrand Aristide asks France to repay $21,685,135,571.48. France rejects it.

modernEvents.title: HIPC debt relief
modernEvents.text: Haiti reaches the HIPC completion point: about $1.2 billion of relief from HIPC and MDRI.

modernEvents.title: Earthquake debt relief
modernEvents.text: After the January 2010 earthquake, the IMF cancels $268 million of Haiti’s debt; other lenders follow.

modernEvents.title: PetroCaribe settlement
modernEvents.text: In January 2024 Haiti pays $500 million and Venezuela forgives $1.69 billion of PetroCaribe debt.
